items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: It was my good friend. Bill Rosso.

ctx.x: Did you, when you came back from time to time, did you have any fans ever in the 40s for, you know, just to say a one night job? Or would you appear as a guest any time?

The only time I became interested in playing my horn again is when Joe Moray is asking me to come and make the Southland record. I had stopped playing all together and just laid the horn down. But when this came about, and no, I'll have to go back a little further. What's his name over at the Preservation Hall that takes the interview? It was my good friend. Bill Rosso. He plays the violin.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: I think I recall telling Bill Russell an incident about Buddy and I.

ctx.x: You said you knew Buddy Petit?

Oh yes, I was a very good friend to Buddy. I think I recall telling Bill Russell an incident about Buddy and I. I used to play on this boat they call the Susquehanna. I don't know if you can recall that. You probably weren't nowhere around New Orleans. I read the name. You read the name? Yeah. Well the Susquehanna would leave Spanish Fort and go across the lake and it would dock over in, what's the name of the little town over there? Vanderville? Northern. Covington? Covington. And the doctor, it would dock there…
Do you remember anything about his style? Like you know, was he a high note man?

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: Yes, he's never heard of it. He didn't know he was in San Antonio.

ctx.x: Let me ask you about the Bill Johnson. You must have mentioned that to Don Alba, huh?

Yes, he's never heard of it. He didn't know he was in San Antonio. So Don, of course, is light enough to pass, too. He wouldn't have to be afraid to talk to Don, but he's passing, evidently. But with that age and his memory gone, evidently.
